scope: Actual native rename candidate RPC with acknowledged-catalog/input/scope binding, bounded off-owner metadata/analysis/proof/framing and final owner publication fences

verification.nativeOrchestrationRun: PASS rename candidate orchestration: 41 checks; actual worker frame, original post-frame disk identity, encoding failure, cancellation versus physical quiescence, detached inputs and read-only native candidate

evidenceNotes: The actual server dispatches xlang/renameCandidate, advertises experimental.renameCandidate1 only for native backends and preserves standard rename/applyEdit inactivity. Positive success envelopes now traverse the actual IDE owner/worker/stdio connection and existing strict edit-call router.

A new bounded orchestration worker retains decoded intent, independently acknowledged catalog and immutable document snapshots. It strictly compares configuration/input receipt, reconstructs complete project/standalone scope, rejects omitted open documents and uses the actual native cursor/reference pipeline. No submit-time source-body copy/hash, compiler or filesystem work.

Proof export and outer JSON-RPC response framing occur on the orchestration worker. The original complete native guard set is swept again after final framing, including unchanged providers. The protocol owner only gates original document identity/version/input serial/config epoch and queued input before writing already encoded bytes.

Individual request cancellation propagates to the worker/native query. Lease acquisition cancels pending work and requires both physical orchestration and reference-worker quiescence. A controlled real-frame wrapper proves future cancellation is not physical idle and detects identical-byte disk replacement after encoding.

Thirty-five actual stdio cases cover four scopes, imported/qualified/standalone selection, UTF8/BOM/CRLF and signed version extremes, exact bindings and rejection forms, real document changes, same-version close/reopen, config epoch changes, cancellation, lease resume, positive integer IDs, native-backend restriction and absence of standard rename.

The first protocol helper runs29 cases but incorrectly treats the intentionally rejected equal-version didChange stderr line as failure. The corrected and expanded final35-case helper accepts only that exact expected diagnostic. Its passed execution, complete transcripts and protected-file identities are authoritative; the earlier raw failure is retained.

Eight separately compiled actual mutants are rejected: omit final post-frame source sweep, bypass acknowledged catalog/input receipt/open-root coverage/version checks, alter reply token, manufacture physical idle, or bypass server publication fences. Final interpreted protocol fixtures and the exact native assertion program are bound to the final executions. Compile failures and crashes do not count.

Full110-unit native and131-unit matched GUI rebuilds use current public headers. Existing native proof/source/provider/recheck and50 protocol cases pass. Actual IDE167 checks now require a real positive candidate while preserving C/xlang typing/delete/undo/IME/focus and original source bytes. Full55 GUI suites and two24-frame rendered captures pass.

All actual source/header compilation closures, compiled/link inputs and72 raw core-archive member payloads are bound. Normal runtime binaries, the developer SDK, the active delivery index and required user temporary directories remain unchanged.
limits: Candidate remains untrusted until the client independently approves native source guards, provider/member coverage, static result and WorkspaceEdit. No automatic result controller or standard rename UI is enabled.
Client negotiated activation and protocol cancellation sending, physical file/alias policy, owned-write fences, transaction host, confirmation, recovery and standard rename/applyEdit remain open.

Full generic/unbound/foreign qualification, latest engine asset alignment, other synchronous readers, deep unprefixed xlp paths, analysis-configuration cache-count regression and whole-goal performance/resource/longevity qualification remain open.

The existing stdout writer remains owner-serialized bounded blocking I/O. Worker proof/framing placement is not a claim of fully asynchronous transport, whole-IDE latency/RSS, complete internal allocator-failure testing or zero overhead.

Existing candidate/frame/context/graph/cache quotas apply; queued decoded intents, shared snapshots, DOM/codec/allocator/library work, active compiler data and OS resources are additional. Retained-byte quotas are not process memory limits.
C LSP stays disabled. No DAP/debug/runtime completion or Linux/sanitizer qualification in this stage.
